Videos Meridian Polaris is a dynamic medium-gain overdrive, with incredibly flexible tone-shaping capabilities. Its unique feature set includes an optional 2-pole resonant filter, controllable via expression pedal for filter sweeps and out-of-this-world overdrive tones. Designed to help you explore the outer-limits of harmonic overdrive, Polaris’s Drive control goes from just a touch of harmonics to full-tilt, live-wire overdrive on the brink of distortion, while staying reactive to your instrument and dynamics for an experience that’s addicting. EXTREME TONE SHAPING The shining beacon of Polaris is contained within the unique tone shaping center at the heart of its control panel. Four out of the six controls are purely for tonal adjustments. The Filter control is the star of the show, an extremely effective control with three filter options, selectable via the Depth toggle switch above it. First position is a standard, single-pole low pass filter to adjust the high-end content. In the middle, you’ll find a deeper 2-pole filter for serious sculpting. Last and certainly far from least, is the 2-pole resonant filter for the most extreme shaping. The Bass toggle switch offers three options for keeping your low frequencies under control. Whether you need a tasteful bass cut or boost, or you simply want them untouched, Polaris has you covered. The Initial control blends in your raw, pre-filtered overdrive tone. Using this control in conjunction with the Filter control allows for serious tone shaping, by re-introducing the raw signal to balance more extreme Filter settings. EXPRESS YOURSELF All three filter options are fully sweep-able via the EXP jack, using a standard TRS expression pedal or expression device, opening the door to inspiring movement within your overdrive tones. In addition, Polaris is fully compatible with Mission Control for interstellar filter sweeps and dirty auto-filter effects. POLARIS FEATURES FIlter control with 3 depths, all fully sweepable via expression pedal Three position BASS toggle switch for low-end control A smooth, symmetrical clipping style overdrive with a detailed texture True-Bypass switching via soft-click footswitch Requires external 9v DC power supply (center-negative) A CADET SERIES PEDAL The Cadet Series brings Spaceman’s signature sonic character to a wider audience through repeatable, SMD-based designs. Classic Spaceman designs with the same attention to tone and detail, these pedals offer consistent availability, accessible pricing, and everyday reliability - without sacrificing the individuality that defines Spaceman. Screen printed faceplates and raw metal enclosures set this series apart. Ideal for working musicians and pedalboard-ready setups, the Cadet Series is where our craft meets practicality. the Polaris and Sputnik III Oct 30, 2025 15:00 by  Stefan Karlsson Boost Boost and Overdrive Fuzz Germanium Fuzz Harmonic Overdrive Overdrive Spaceman Effects + - I’ve detailed before how Spaceman Effects has various series of pedals at different price points - NOS Series (entirely hand-made THT), Standard Series (Hybrid SMT + THT), and the Affordable Cadet Series (Machine-made SMT) - there are further nuances - somewhat further conflated now by a PDX Custom Series, and a Mod Series. For me I’m mostly concerned with the style of components and the process of manufacture. The machine-made flow-line Cadet series - is by far and away the most affordable Spaceman pedals you can buy. You can see here that the Cadet Polaris is just $199, and the Cadet Sputnik III is at $219 - where originally those were at $319 to $399 and $269 to $399 respectively - for different editions. Available of course from the Spaceman Effect Webstore and leading International Dealers. The Sputnik III was the first Spaceman pedal to split into Standard and Limited Editions back in 2020 - where the former consisted of the same NOS Germanium Transistors - but the supporting cast of components was SMT-based - versus full-size THT components for the Limited Editions. So the Sputnik III had the most extreme range of pricing at that point - $269 for the Hybrid Standard Version [SMT / THT Mix] (which is what I have), and then up to $399 for the Limited All-THT Editions - the new Cadet Sputnik III is thus $40 more affordable. Actually I’m starting to think that the Standard Hybrid Series - has been replaced by the All-SMT Cadet Series (with the exception of Germanium Transistors and Diodes) - while typically a pedal with THT components will be a limited small batch handmade run! I of course have all the Spaceman Effects pedals that I want - so the Cadet Series comes a little late for my own purposes. The machine-made editions are near enough every bit as good as the far more pricier Limited Editions - for anyone thinking of dipping their toes into Spaceman Effects - the Cadet Series is the perfect place to start! Both those pedals have been covered numerous times on this site - so I will just reference their controls here, and share with you the original Edition Demos.
